name: Wound-primary current transformer
summary: CT with a primary winding of several turns, used for low primary currents where a bar primary gives too little accuracy.
description: A wound-primary CT has a primary winding of more than one turn rather than a single bar or conductor through a window. This is needed at low primary currents, where a single turn would not produce enough magnetising ampere-turns for accurate metering, and it is common in MV metering units.

The wound primary has a lower short-time withstand than a bar primary, so its thermal and dynamic ratings need checking against the fault level. The symbol shows the winding but not those ratings, which belong in the CT schedule.
readingNotes: Check the short-time thermal rating against the fault level.
Read primary terminals P1 and P2 for polarity.
distinction: A wound-primary CT has a multi-turn primary; a window or bar CT uses the circuit conductor as a single-turn primary.
